title: Design Intent Verification Artifact
description: Machine-generated verification result for one Design Intent Record, written to design-intent/.verification/<surface-id>.earl.json during a CI run and never committed. EARL-shaped vocabulary reuse only; this is not an EARL, RDF, or JSON-LD conformance claim.

schemaVersion.description: Contract version of this generated artifact.

surfaceId.description: Equals the artifact filename stem and the authored record's surfaceId.

intentDigest.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the authored record's UTF-8 content after CRLF-to-LF normalization. Proves which authored revision these results describe.

assertedBy.description: Tool or runner that produced these results.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time of generation. The validator parses this semantically because the schema engine does not enforce the date-time format.

assertions.description: Exactly one assertion per authored expectation.

outcome.description: EARL-derived outcome vocabulary. Always the observed probe result; an authored override never replaces it.

effectiveOutcome.description: Contract-level effective outcome. Either observed or human failed yields failed; a human pass settles only unresolved observations; otherwise the observed outcome remains. This is the value the gate applies.

overrideConflict.description: True only when observed outcome and authored override outcome are each passed or failed and differ. A human override that settles an untested, cantTell, or inapplicable expectation is not a conflict.

pointer.description: Optional location of the evidence, such as a selector or source reference.

info.description: Optional machine-generated detail. Required and non-empty when the outcome is inapplicable.

allOf.$comment: An inapplicable result must say why it did not apply.

assertion.$comment: No human-authored field appears here. 'outcome' records observedOutcome only. 'effectiveOutcome' applies fail-safe precedence across observation and authored override. 'overrideConflict' marks a conclusive disagreement between observed and authored outcomes.
